104	/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
105	def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
106	  (List.range n).map fun k =>
107	    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
108	      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
109	    f k t

111	/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
112	    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
113	def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
114	  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
115	  | some first, some last =>
116	    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
117	    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
118	    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
119	    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
120	    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
121	    pre ++ τ ++ post
122	  | _, _ => τ
123	
124	def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ
125	
126	/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
127	def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
128	  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
129	  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

131	end Build
132	
133	/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
134	    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
135	    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
136	    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
137	    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
138	    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
139	    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
140	    far enough to decide it. -/
141	structure Scenario where
142	  name : String
143	  rule : String
144	  trace : Trace
145	  reading : Reading
146	  manifest : Manifest
147	  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
148	  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
149	  expected : Verdict
150	  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
151	  boundary : String := ""
152	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
153	
154	namespace Scenario
155	/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
156	    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
157	def pastOps : List String :=
158	  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
159	   "heading_since"]
160	
161	/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
162	    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
163	    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
164	    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
165	    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
166	    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
167	    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
168	    `unknown` witness only.
169	    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
170	    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
171	def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
172	  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
173	  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
174	    | some r => pure r
175	    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
176	  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
177	    | .ok S => pure S
178	    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
179	  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
180	    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
181	      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
182	  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
183	  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
184	  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
185	    match sc.window with
186	    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
187	    | none => true
188	  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
189	  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
190	    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
191	  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
192	    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
193	  match sc.expected with
194	  | .notApplicable =>
195	    if tl.present then pure got
196	    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
197	  | .unknown _ =>
198	    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
199	    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
200	    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
201	      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
202	      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
203	    if !stray.isEmpty then
204	      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
205	    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
206	      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
207	    else pure got
208	  | _ => pure got
209	end Scenario
210	
211	end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.

  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.

  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
  writes through a `Units` constructor.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Build

/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))

def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)

/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track
    classes := some classes
    kin := { position := some pos
             heading := some heading
             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
             speed := some speed
             extent := some halfExtent
             pathLength := pathLength } }

/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }

def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }

/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]

    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)

  { id := id
    kind := .lane

                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
                   entersIntersection := enters } }

  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }

def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }

  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }

  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }

    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=

  users.flatMap fun u =>

    | none => []

      | none => none

def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
  { t := t
    subject := subject
    users := users
    structures := structures
    devices := devices
    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
    env := env
    assumptions := assumptions
    intents := intents }

/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
  (List.range n).map fun k =>
    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    f k t

/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
  | some first, some last =>
    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
    pre ++ τ ++ post
  | _, _ => τ

def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ

/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

end Build

/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
    far enough to decide it. -/
structure Scenario where
  name : String
  rule : String
  trace : Trace
  reading : Reading
  manifest : Manifest
  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
  expected : Verdict
  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
  boundary : String := ""
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace Scenario
/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
def pastOps : List String :=
  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
   "heading_since"]

/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
    `unknown` witness only.
    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
    | .ok S => pure S
    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
    match sc.window with
    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
    | none => true
  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
  match sc.expected with
  | .notApplicable =>
    if tl.present then pure got
    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
  | .unknown _ =>
    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
    if !stray.isEmpty then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
    else pure got
  | _ => pure got
end Scenario

end TrafficSpec

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

  Geometry (every figure is the witness's own and appears nowhere in the rule):
  - approach lane 10: x ∈ [-40, 0] m, y ∈ [-2, 2] m, direction east, entering intersection 20;
  - intersection 20: x ∈ [0, 10] m, y ∈ [-10, 10] m;
  - traffic signal 30 governing lane 10; what it displays is the scenario's.
  - subject, track 1, a motor vehicle, half-length 2 m, half-width 1 m; sampled every 50 ms
    (the carla_scene_graph rate), 25 scenes, t = 0 … 1200 ms. Its reference point advances
    0.72 m a scene, x = -3.44 + 0.72·k m: front reaches the intersection at k = 2 (entry: it
    occupies the lane and the intersection), rear leaves the lane after k = 7 and the
    intersection after k = 21 (exit at k = 22, t = 1100 ms). Occupancy is stated per scene, since
    the body spans two regions at the entry.
  - The heading change through the intersection is carried by the yaw rate, set at every scene
    from the entry to the exit (k = 2 … 22, 20 intervals of 50 ms, 1 s): 0 deg/s straight through,
    90 deg/s for a 90° left turn, -90 deg/s for a 90° right turn, 180 deg/s for a reversal. The
    position track is kept straight; the turn concepts read the yaw rate only.
  - Every witness speaks about t = 50 … 1200 ms (`window`): the exit and entry edges (`rises`) are
    unobserved at the first scene.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_307_4a_o1
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_307_4a_o1

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: subject ↦ 1

def laneId : RegionId := 10
def interId : RegionId := 20
def signalId : DeviceId := 30

def approach : Structure :=
  Build.lane laneId [(m (-40), m (-2)), (m 0, m (-2)), (m 0, m 2), (m (-40), m 2)] Build.east
    (enters := some interId)

def intersection : Structure := Build.rect interId .intersection (m 0) (m (-10)) (m 10) (m 10)

/-- The subject's reference point at scene `k`. -/
def posAt (k : Nat) : Vec := (cm (72 * (k : Int) - 344), m 0)

/-- What the subject occupies at scene `k`. -/
def occAt (k : Nat) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
  (if k ≤ 7 then [(1, laneId)] else []) ++ (if 2 ≤ k && k ≤ 21 then [(1, interId)] else [])

/-- A passage through the intersection under a signal displaying `showsAt k`, with yaw rate `yaw`
    from the entry to the exit. -/
def passage (showsAt : Nat → List SignalIndication) (yaw : Q) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 25 0 (Units.milliseconds 50) fun k t =>
    let yr := if 2 ≤ k && k ≤ 22 then yaw else Q.zero
    let u := Build.withKin
      (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (posAt k) Build.east (cm 1440) (m 2, m 1, cm 75))
      fun kn => { kn with yawRate := some yr }
    Build.scene t (some 1) [u] [approach, intersection] [Build.signal signalId [laneId] (showsAt k)]
      (occupies := some (occAt k))

/-- `forbid` (violated): The subject vehicle enters an intersection from an approach lane whose dev.traffic_signal displays green_arrow(left) alone and drives straight through: at its exit drv.motion.left_turn_through_region does not hold (heading change about 0 degrees). No other road user is in the scene. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .left]) (Units.degrees 0)

/-- `permit` (compliant): The same subject turns left through the intersection on the green left arrow alone: at its exit the heading change since its entry is about 90 degrees to the left. -/
def permitTrace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .left]) (Units.degrees 90)

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green alone throughout its passage; the subject drives straight through. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.circularGreen]) (Units.degrees 0)

/-- `blind` (unknown): The subject passes through the intersection on a green left arrow alone, but its yaw rate is not observed: the turn concepts cannot be decided at its exit. -/
def blindTrace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .left]) (Units.degrees 0)

/-- `occasion_s1` (violated): The signal displays green_arrow(left) alone when the subject enters the intersection and changes to yellow_arrow(left) while the subject is inside; the subject drives straight through: the arrow was displayed alone for part of the passage only. -/
def occasion_s1Trace : Trace :=
  passage (fun k => if k ≤ 5 then [.greenArrow .left] else [.yellowArrow .left]) (Units.degrees 0)

/-- `occasion_s1_outside` (not_applicable): The signal displays green_arrow(left) alone only before the subject enters the intersection and circular_red from its entry to its exit; the subject drives straight through: the arrow held only before the passage began. -/
def occasion_s1_outsideTrace : Trace :=
  passage (fun k => if k ≤ 1 then [.greenArrow .left] else [.circularRed]) (Units.degrees 0)

/-- `branch_1` (compliant): green_arrow(right) alone; the subject turns 90° right through the intersection. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .right]) (Units.degrees (-90))

/-- `branch_2` (compliant): green_arrow(u_turn) alone; the subject reverses direction (180°) through the intersection. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .uTurn]) (Units.degrees 180)

/-- `branch_3` (not_applicable): green_arrow(left) shown together with circular_red, so not alone; the subject drives straight through. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace := passage (fun _ => [.greenArrow .left, .circularRed]) (Units.degrees 0)

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_307_4a_o1"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("subject", 1)]
    expected := expected
    window := some (50, 1200)
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["kin.yaw_rate"]
  , witness "occasion_s1" occasion_s1Trace .violated
  , witness "occasion_s1_outside" occasion_s1_outsideTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .notApplicable ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_307_4a_o1

/-
  TRAINING SPLIT variant, generated by harness/tools/split.py from the full file: the lines that read the
  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.

  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.

  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.

  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Grounding
open Semantics

/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
structure Grounding where
  assign : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
  let c := canon cm
  { s with
    subject := s.subject.map c
    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
structure Setup where
  rules : List Rule
  d : Primitives.Ctx

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.

  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec

/-- π to seven digits (355/113), for the heading vectors only. -/
def piQ : Q := Q.mk' 355 113

/-- (sin x, cos x) by their Taylor series, x in radians, |x| ≤ π. -/
def sinCos (x : Q) : Q × Q := Id.run do
  let x2 := Q.mul x x
  let mut c := Q.ofInt 1
  let mut s := x
  let mut tc := Q.ofInt 1
  let mut ts := x
  for n in [1:16] do
    tc := Q.neg (Q.div (Q.mul tc x2) (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat ((2 * n - 1) * (2 * n)))))
    ts := Q.neg (Q.div (Q.mul ts x2) (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)))))
    c := Q.add c tc
    s := Q.add s ts
  return (s, c)

/-- A quantity floored to 10⁻⁹. -/
def roundNano (q : Q) : Q := Q.mk' ((q.num * 1000000000) / (q.den : Int)) 1000000000

/-- The unit heading at `deg` degrees counter-clockwise from east. -/
def headingAt (deg : Q) : Vec :=
  let sc := sinCos (Q.div (Q.mul deg piQ) (Q.ofInt 180))
  (roundNano sc.2, roundNano sc.1)

/-- The yaw rate at scene `k`: held over the interval before the scene, from the one after the
    entry (k = 3) to the exit (k = 22). -/
def yawAt (yaw : Q) (k : Nat) : Q := if 3 ≤ k && k ≤ 22 then yaw else Q.zero

/-- The heading angle at scene `k` (degrees from east): the yaw rate integrated over 50 ms
    intervals, each interval taking the rate of the scene that ends it. -/
def angleAt (yaw : Q) (k : Nat) : Q :=
  let turned : Nat := if k ≤ 2 then 0 else if k ≤ 22 then k - 2 else 20
  Q.mul yaw (Q.mul (Units.milliseconds 50) (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat turned)))

/-- The subject's reference point at scene `k`: 0.72 m a scene along the heading of the scene
    that ends each interval. -/
def posAt (yaw : Q) : Nat → Vec
  | 0 => (cm (-344), m 0)
  | k + 1 =>
    let p := posAt yaw k
    let u := headingAt (angleAt yaw (k + 1))
    (Q.add p.1 (Q.mul (cm 72) u.1), Q.add p.2 (Q.mul (cm 72) u.2))

/-- What the subject occupies at scene `k`. -/
def occAt (k : Nat) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
  (if k ≤ 7 then [(1, laneId)] else []) ++ (if 2 ≤ k && k ≤ 21 then [(1, interId)] else [])

/-- A passage through the intersection under a signal displaying `showsAt k`, with yaw rate `yaw`
    from the entry to the exit. -/
def passage (showsAt : Nat → List SignalIndication) (yaw : Q) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 25 0 (Units.milliseconds 50) fun k t =>
    let u := Build.withKin
      (Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] (posAt yaw k) (headingAt (angleAt yaw k)) (cm 1440) (m 2, m 1, cm 75))
      fun kn => { kn with yawRate := some (yawAt yaw k) }

**Final verdict: OK** (9 witnesses, 11 names, composes nothing)

1. `UNUSED_CLAIM` — an accidental run on the untouched skeleton (I wrapped the gate command in a pipe by mistake), before I had written anything. Nothing changed because of it.

Fix: the heading vectors now follow the yaw rate. Each interval turns by the rate of the scene that ends it. The vectors come from a Taylor series with π ≈ 355/113, floored to 10⁻⁹. Positions now advance 0.72 m per scene along the heading.
4. `OK`.

- Class: `ru_aggregate subject DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic` ∧ `ru_aggregate subject DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle`.
- Occasion (event): the rule is judged when the subject exits intersection `i`: `rises (¬ rel_occupies subject i)`. The act starts at the latest entry, `rises (rel_occupies subject i)`. The stretch from entry to exit is written as `since (¬ rises occ_i) …`, which stops at the latest entry and cannot reach an earlier passage.
- s2: carrier `c` (`travel_region`) with `st_lane_enters c i`, occupied by the subject at the entry. Traffic signal `d` with `dev_governs d c`.
- s1, read at `some_moment` in [entry, exit]: `since (¬rises occ_i) (arrowAlone dir ∧ since (¬rises occ_i) (rises occ_i ∧ occ_c))`, for dir ∈ {left, right, u_turn}.
- s3: at the exit, the turn concept for the arrow's direction must hold over `i`, with the node's parameters. The u-turn concept takes only the step and `p.u_turn_heading_min`.
- Obligation: the applicability's whole selection (i, c, d, dir) is restated, and for that selection the passage must match the arrow's direction.

## Choices the node left open
- **"Alone"**: the green arrow is shown and none of the other concrete states of the enumeration is shown (all circular and flashing states, `dark`, every other arrow). If the head shows `unknown` (a face the source could not read), I don't treat the arrow as decidedly not alone. Instead the arrow is wrapped in `definedWhen (¬ shows unknown)`, so the result is unknown. This follows the three-valued rule that unobserved is never false. It is not a narrowing: s1 is a trigger and is carried as written.
- **Quantifier over selections**: the obligation is existential over (i, c, d, dir). I took this from the record's own words ("Re-binding i, c, d and dir with the whole selection … matching any one of them complies"), so I declared no narrowing. One point for review: `st.lane_enters` says a rule never picks the carrier that favours the road user. If the subject occupied two approach carriers at entry with different signals, the existential choice could favour the subject. The record does not separate that case. None of the witnesses has it.

- U-turn arrow with a U-turn (compliant);
